subject: Request: detailed subprocessor roster and onward transfer permission — MediCore DPA
messages:
From: Jessica Liu <jessica.liu@medicore.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Oakridge Procurement <procurement@oakridgehealth.org>
Date: 2026-11-15T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Subprocessor roster + onward transfer question for DPA renewal

Hi Sean,

MediCore is starting our annual vendor reassessment ahead of the DPA renewal. Two quick asks for our compliance team by EOD 2026-11-22: 1) the up-to-date subprocessor roster including hosting, analytics, and any marketplace/reseller partners, and 2) confirmation whether Redwood permits onward transfers to marketplace/reseller partners (specifically a vendor called "Marketplace Ops") under your standard DPA.

Because MediCore is a HIPAA-covered entity, we also need to understand whether any of the subprocessors will have access to PHI (directly or via encrypted tokens) and whether you maintain a signed BAAs or equivalent safeguards with those subprocessors. If any subprocessors rely on SCCs or other transfer mechanisms, please flag that too.

If helpful, we can accept a short CSV and the relevant certs (SOC 2, CAIQ snapshot). Attaching the procurement contact so they can coordinate PO updates if necessary.

Thanks — tight timeline on our side.

Jessica Liu
Compliance Manager, MediCore Health
jessica.liu@medicore.com
+1 415 555 0134

Subject: Re: Subprocessor roster + onward transfer question for DPA renewal

Hi Jessica — thanks for the clear list. We'll get you a current roster and certs by EOD Monday (2026-11-16). Quick clarifications while we gather artifacts:

- Marketplace Ops is listed as a reseller/integration partner we work with for optional third-party marketplace listings; they do not host model weights or persistent customer data by default.
- By default Redwood does not share unredacted PHI with resellers unless a customer enables a marketplace integration; we'll call that out explicitly.
- We will include whether we maintain BAAs or equivalent contractual safeguards with each subprocessor and whether SCCs are in place for EU transfers.

Attaching our current roster snapshot and SOC 2 Type II for ease of review. Also linking the DPA (v3) and the HubSpot deal for your reference.

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.example.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.example.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.example.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T14:20:00-05:00
Subject: FW: Subprocessor roster + onward transfer question for DPA renewal

Looping legal/ops in. Quick note on next steps from a Contracts perspective:

- We should mark Marketplace Ops as a "marketplace/reseller" subprocessor and confirm whether we require customers to opt in to any data sharing. If Marketplace Ops only receives metadata or encrypted tokens, that's different than receiving PHI.
- For MediCore (HIPAA) we need an explicit statement from them on whether they will send PHI to any downstream integration. If yes, we must ensure either (a) Redwood has executed a written agreement with that subprocessor that satisfies BAA-equivalent obligations, or (b) we prohibit onward transfer unless an addendum is signed.
- Recommend drafting a short DPA addendum that grants conditional onward transfer permission when: (i) customer explicitly opts in to the marketplace integration, (ii) Redwood confirms subprocessor safeguards (SOC2 + technical controls), and (iii) subprocessor signatory executes our standard subprocessor agreement or BAA.

I'll prepare a one-page addendum template and the DocuSign envelope ID. Monica — please confirm whether we can use SCCs for CloudMarketPlace transfers for EU customers; if not, we'll add a restriction.

Action items: Priya to draft addendum (ETA 2026-11-16 morning). Monica to confirm SCC posture. Rishi/Evelyn to supply the technical controls summary we can call out.

-Priya
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.example.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.example.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.example.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2026-11-16T09:42:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor roster + onward transfer question for DPA renewal

Adding technical detail for the record and for inclusion in the addendum:

- SOC 2 Type II available (attached). CAIQ snapshot available on request.
- Marketplace Ops integration operates as a "brokered" connection: they may receive metadata and ephemeral tokens used to initiate a session but do not receive model weights, persistent KV cache, or unencrypted customer content unless the customer explicitly configures an integration that shares content.
- For HIPAA customers: default system behavior is to redact or disallow forwarding of PHI to third-party integrations. We can enable an opt-in flag for an account to allow integrations that might surface PHI — this state change requires a signed addendum.

Attachment: SOC2-TypeII-Redwood-2026.pdf (confidential cert, 1.8MB)

Rishi — please add the short technical bulleted list of controls we can publish in the addendum (encryption in transit/at rest, access controls, logging, retention limits).

-Evelyn
Director of Security, Redwood Inference
From: Jessica Liu <jessica.liu@medicore.com>

Thanks for the quick responses and the roster. To confirm MediCore's position: we will NOT enable marketplace integrations that would transmit PHI to third parties. MediCore will only use any optional integrations for metadata or anonymized telemetry.

Given that, please proceed with the conditional addendum approach you suggested and route it for DocuSign. MediCore's procurement will sign the addendum and the PO once the legal and technical controls are clearly documented. I can share the draft PO after review — attaching a placeholder here for reference.

Attachment: medi_core_po_4672.pdf (placeholder)

Regards,
Jessica
